subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & model recs (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — long-context evals

Hey John / Priya — great to meet today, thanks for the detailed walkthrough of the Acme use case. Recap below and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap (quick):
- Primary objective: automatic summarization + entity-extraction on documents up to ~150k tokens (legal bundles, technical specs).
- Key constraints: low tolerance for hallucination, preservation of nested structure, and a small number of multi-document summarizations per minute (bursty).
- Current infra: on-prem storage; we can pull a sample set for evaluation under your security controls.

Recommended next steps (from Redwood):
1) Share prompt set + sample long-docs (attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx).
2) Redwood runs a pilot evaluation (10–20 long-doc summarizations) measuring: ROUGE-L, factuality checks, and truncation incidents.
3) We'll propose recommended models/configs and an MAP (mutual action plan) with timelines and success criteria.

Initial model guidance (high-level):
- Try a long-context-optimized variant: "redwood-long-13b" for best fidelity at 150k tokens (we have a 128k and a 256k profile we can leverage).
- For cost-sensitive evals: a 2.7B long-context quantized variant (rw-long-2.7b-q4) to validate latency/throughput tradeoffs.

Attachments: redwood_long_context_benchmarks_v1.pdf (preliminary bench), acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx

Can you confirm:
- A safe sample set (anonymized) for Redwood to ingest?
- Target SLA for the pilot (results expected by Nov 10?)

I'll loop in engineering (Michael) and product (Neha) on technical details once you confirm.

Thanks — Marissa

1) Truncation behavior: our documents can be up to ~200k tokens when you include attachments/embedded exhibits. How does Redwood handle truncation for the 128k profile vs the 256k? Is there automatic chunking + stitching or do we need to implement a client-side chunker?

2) Summarization fidelity / hallucination: can you share example outputs (on a redacted doc) demonstrating fidelity differences between the 13B long model and the 2.7B quantized variant? We want to see concrete tradeoffs on hallucination rate and omission of key clauses.

3) Timing: we can provide an anonymized sample set by EOD Friday (30 Oct). If Redwood can run the 10-sample pilot by Nov 10, that would be ideal. Any constraints on on-prem sample ingestion (SFTP / signed SCP / secure Drive link)?

Priya and I are copied — we prefer a short follow-up demo after the pilot to review outputs with legal and eng.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — long-context evals

Great questions — answers below, plus what we'll run in the pilot.

1) Truncation & chunking:
- For the 128k profile we use windowed KV-cache stitching with optional overlap; for docs > window size we support two approaches: server-side sliding-chunk + stitched summary, or client-side chunking where you control chunk boundaries. Server-side stitching is simpler for you; it will attempt to preserve order and recover entity chains, but we log "truncation incidents" when a section is dropped.
- The 256k profile reduces the need to chunk, but does increase GPU memory and cost. For initial evals we recommend using the 128k profile with server-side stitching and a conservative overlap (1–2k tokens) so we can measure fidelity vs cost.

2) Fidelity examples: attached sample outputs (acme_sample_outputs.zip) are redacted excerpts from prior long-context pilots. High level: 13B-long preserves nested clause references much better; 2.7B-q4 tends to be stronger at surface-level summaries but misses low-frequency clauses more often. We'll include a short table of hallucination rates (automated fact-check + manual spot checks) in the benchmark PDF.

3) Secure ingestion: SFTP is fine; we can also accept a signed Google Drive share under a narrow ACL (preferred for ease). For on-prem air-gapped customers we provide an appliance-based runner — not needed here unless you request.

Pilot plan (what Redwood will deliver):
- Ingest 10 anonymized long-docs (you provide via secure Drive/SFTP).
- Run three model variants: redwood-long-13b (256k/128k profile), rw-long-2.7b-q4 (128k profile), plus a distilled baseline (rw-1.3b) to set expectations.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, atomic hallucination rate (automated + manual), truncation incidents, throughput (s/doc) and cost estimate.
- Deliverables: detailed report (benchmarks + example outputs), recommended config, and a 45-min results walkthrough.

I've attached the updated benchmark report and the prompt set. If EOD Friday for the sample set works, we'll schedule the pilot this week and aim to have preliminary outputs by Nov 9 to allow the Nov 10 review.

Next step: Can you confirm the transfer method (SFTP vs Drive) and the preferred time for the walkthrough (Nov 10 morning PT or afternoon)?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: pilot considerations / notes for Acme

Internal notes — sending to Marissa + Neha (do not forward externally):
- For the pilot we should enable prefix caching on repeated legal boilerplate to reduce token spend; add a flag in the job to enable KV-prefetch for exhibits that are reused across docs.
- Validation harness: we'll include automated atomicity checks (entity consistency across chunks) and a small manual spot-check workflow for legal SME review. Plan to run both automated and manual checks so we can provide a hallucination confidence interval.
- Logging: capture truncation incidents as structured logs with context_id for each doc to make root-cause analysis easy during the walkthrough.
- Resource note: 13B with 256k window requires pinned GPUs; confirm capacity with infra (I can escalate if the pilot window conflicts with other reserved runs).

I'll prepare the evaluation job spec and a lightweight dashboard mock for the Nov 10 walkthrough.

— Michael
